target: show that the R44I 2^w exact universal-state barrier can be bypassed on structured boundary languages by switching representation instead of quotienting arbitrary assignments

machine.input: a boundary interaction recognized exactly as a system A x = b over GF(2)
machine.representation: reduced row echelon form with provenance
machine.exact_semantics: the represented solution set is exactly the set of boundary assignments satisfying A x = b
machine.composition: conjoin interfaces by stacking equations and reducing again over GF(2)
machine.query: consistency and implication questions are answered by Gaussian elimination without enumerating all 2^w boundary assignments
machine.size_bound: O(w^2) bits for a dense w-variable row-reduced matrix plus provenance overhead polynomial in explicit input size

relation_to_R44I.explanation: R44I rules out merging arbitrary boundary assignments into a context-independent exact quotient for unrestricted future continuations. R44J instead changes the represented object: for a recognized affine interaction it stores the exact set of all compatible assignments symbolically as linear equations.

promotion_rule.allowed_claim: structured exact representation can replace exponential assignment enumeration on the recognized affine class
forbidden_claims: every 3CNF has a polynomial-size exact boundary signature
